clips.environment: Pre-dawn interior of a Macedonian command tent at the Gaugamela camp: lamplight and a brazier, canvas walls, a simple cot. Two armed Macedonian guards stand motionless over the sleeping man. FIRST FRAME already shows this strange image.
clips.scene: LINEAR OPEN, hook front-loaded. Hazel whispers to her own lens while armed guards watch a sleeping man by lamplight; she glances back at the cot mid-line; the last ~3 seconds HOLD on her slow deadpan into the lens, no words.
clips.dialogue: HAZEL (whisper): "Gaugamela. 331 BC. Tonight, an empire two hundred and twenty years old gets a new owner — and the man who's about to take it—" (glance back at the cot) "—is still asleep." Alexander sleeps; he never speaks.
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens, arm's length, slight natural sway; the cot with the sleeping king readable behind her over her shoulder. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER asleep per his lock; Hazel scribe wardrobe established here and locked for the episode; guards' Macedonian gear only.
clips.sound: Tent-canvas rustle, distant camp murmur, brazier tick, her whisper.
clips.endingState: Her held deadpan filling frame, eyes to lens; cot and guards unchanged behind her.

clips.environment: Same command tent, minutes later; lamplight, first grey pre-dawn light at the tent flap.
clips.stillComposition: The instant Parmenion bursts in and shakes the waking king awake — Parmenion's hand gripping Alexander's shoulder, mid-shout, weight forward and tense. Alexander is caught mid-rise from the cot, one hand reaching toward his sword belt, face calm despite being startled awake. Hazel stands a few steps back and to the side, near the tent's edge, watching the exchange with alert attention — a genuine bystander physically present in the room, not narrating to any lens, hands empty at her sides. All three figures fully visible together in one wide external frame: Parmenion and Alexander form the foreground focal action; Hazel is a clear, readable secondary figure in the same space; believable eyelines and blocking; real depth and separation between the three bodies and the tent behind them. CAMERA: a real external observer's framing, eye-level, positioned inside the tent at a natural viewing distance, capturing all three figures together in one frame — no camera, phone, or rig in anyone's hand, no POV distortion, no fisheye, no arm's-length selfie perspective.
clips.scene: Parmenion strides in visibly rattled and shakes the sleeping king awake. Alexander wakes instantly calm, already reaching for his sword belt, unhurried. Mid-scene a wax tablet is pressed into Hazel's hands without explanation; she fumbles the stylus (running-gag plant).
clips.timeline: 0-2s: Parmenion enters, shakes him, speaks. 2-5s: Alexander wakes calm, reaches for sword belt, Parmenion presses his question. 5-8s: Alexander answers while buckling armor, half-amused; the tablet is pressed into Hazel's hands. 8-9s: her fumbled-stylus line.
clips.dialogue: PACING IS EXPLICIT PER CHARACTER AND MUST BE FOLLOWED EXACTLY — do not apply one uniform tempo across this exchange; the contrast between Parmenion's urgency and Alexander's unhurried calm IS the scene's performance point, sustained the whole 9 seconds, not just on isolated lines. PARMENION (fast, clipped, breathless with urgency, shaking him): "My lord. MY LORD." — the second "MY LORD" louder and sharper than the first, no space between his two lines. PARMENION (still fast, words tumbling just behind his own movement, worked up): "You could have taken them in the dark last night. Why do you STILL refuse a night attack?" ALEXANDER (EXTREMELY SLOW, unhurried, deliberate, weighty — even while his hands move quickly buckling armor, his VOICE is markedly slower than Parmenion's, with genuine two-second silences between each sentence, never rushed through — match @Audio2's tempo exactly, including its long pauses): "I will not steal a victory, Parmenion." (long two-second pause, no dialogue, just his calm breathing and hands working) "Let it be daylight," (brief pause) "and let it be earned." (another long pause) ALEXANDER (to Hazel, still slow and unhurried, half-amused, not rushed, looking directly at her as he speaks — match @Audio2's tempo): "You write quickly?" HAZEL (HER EYES ARE THE MOST IMPORTANT DETAIL OF THIS BEAT: the instant Alexander's voice turns to address her, her eyes lift OFF THE TABLET and lock onto his face — this eye contact is held, unbroken, for the rest of the shot; she does NOT look back down at the tablet, the stylus, her hands, or anywhere else while she is speaking — a full beat of hesitation before she speaks at all — thrown by the tablet suddenly in her hands, not composed yet; then a dry, slightly startled-amused delivery, unhurried, not swept into the room's urgency, fumbling the stylus by feel without looking at it, her gaze staying on Alexander's face the entire time she talks): "...Apparently—" (small pause) "—as of right now, yes." Only after her line fully ends and a beat passes does she finally look back down at the tablet.
clips.camera: A real external observer's frame inside the tent, all three visible together; the camera holds a natural viewing distance and reframes only to keep the group readable as they move — Parmenion looming over the cot, Alexander rising into it, the tablet pressed into Hazel's hands. EYELINES ARE THE MOST CRITICAL BLOCKING DETAIL IN THIS SHOT AND MUST BE FOLLOWED EXACTLY: when Alexander speaks directly to Hazel ("You write quickly?"), his eyes are on her face, not on the middle distance or on Parmenion. Hazel's eyes are on the tablet ONLY during the brief silent writing beat before Alexander speaks to her — the MOMENT his voice turns toward her, her eyes come UP and lock onto his face, and stay locked on his face through her entire spoken answer; she is never looking down at the tablet, at her hands, off to the side, or at nothing while she is speaking or while he is speaking to her. This is a face-to-face exchange between two people who are looking at each other, not a woman absorbed in writing while a man talks near her. No POV, no selfie framing, nobody's eyeline is the lens. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: Both NPC locks verbatim; the wax diptych tablet and stylus debut here and are tracked for the rest of the episode. Alexander's unhurried pacing here is the same locked trait as every other clip (§32) — this scene does not suspend it, it is the scene that proves it.
clips.sound: Parmenion's footsteps and breath urgent, close, and quick; Alexander's own movements steadier and unhurried under his armor's small-sounds even as his hands work fast; canvas.
clips.endingState: Tablet in her hands, stylus recovered awkwardly; Alexander mid-arming; Parmenion still tense.

clips.dialogue: PACING PER CHARACTER (corrected per short-form retention rule, plus the owner's +20% override on top of the researched bands): Hazel's is easy, curious, unhurried — a genuine question, not rushed, ~198 wpm. Alexander's VOICE conveys unhurried/economical through EMPHASIS and PAUSE PLACEMENT, not through an overall slow rate — his actual word rate is ~156 wpm; the 'unhurried' quality comes from a single deliberate beat of contrast right before his last word, not from a uniformly slow read, even as his HANDS and BODY move fast arming; his vocal pace and his physical pace are deliberately independent of each other, but his voice must never drag or sound sedated. HAZEL (easy, curious, mild wonder, unhurried, ~198 wpm; her eyes on him, watching him arm himself): "What's that?" ALEXANDER (his eyes are LOCKED ONTO THE LEATHER STRAP THREADING THROUGH THE BUCKLE in his own hands — a specific, continuous physical task his gaze tracks the entire line, the same way anyone watches their own hands thread a buckle; his eyes have a physical job to do and that job is not Hazel or the lens; voice measured and economical at ~156 wpm, weight carried by emphasis on "Aristotle's," "corrected," and "dagger," not by slowness): "Homer. Aristotle's own copy — he corrected it himself. Sleeps under my pillow. With the dagger." HAZEL (dry, a small amused edge at the image of a scholar-warrior sleeping with a book and a knife, still unhurried, ~198 wpm; eyes still on him): "You brought a book to a war." ALEXANDER (snapping the last buckle, already moving past her; his voice STAYS measured and economical at ~156 wpm even though his body is now in full motion toward the exit — one deliberate beat of contrast right before the final word "too," not a slow read throughout; his eyes track the buckle and then the sword hilt he checks with his hand as he strides — another continuous physical task, same as the first line — for the whole line UP TO the final word "too"; on "too" specifically, and ONLY on that word, his eyes lift FROM the hilt and land on her for LESS THAN ONE SECOND — a brief flick, not a held gaze — as he passes, then he is gone from frame): "I brought the only book that matters. Achilles didn't get old either. I intend to beat that record too."
clips.camera: Her handheld selfie lens tracking his motion past her; she turns to follow his exit. EYELINES (anchored to physical tasks, not a bare instruction): Alexander's gaze is doing a specific job the whole clip — tracking the strap threading through the buckle on his first line, then the sword hilt his hand checks on his second line — never Hazel, never the lens, because his eyes are occupied with that physical task, not because he's told not to look. The ONE exception: his eyes lift off the hilt and land on her for LESS THAN ONE SECOND, starting only on the word "too" itself, not before it — a brief flick, not a held gaze, then he is already gone from frame; his eyes do NOT hold on her face for multiple seconds or through the words leading up to "too." Hazel's eyes are on him for the entire beat, unbroken — watching him arm himself, then turning to track his exit as he passes her; she never looks away from him. The camera never cuts.
clips.continuity: ALEXANDER lock; motion never stops; scroll-case worn leather.
clips.sound: Armor small-sounds, canvas, distant horses waking.
clips.endingState: Tent flap swinging from his exit; she is turning to follow.

clips.stillComposition: AERIAL CONTINUITY + SCALE FIX v4 (2026-08-29, owner flagged two new issues on v3: (1) scale still not big enough, (2) the Persian side showed a FALSE internal gap — a cluster near the front, then a large stretch of bare open ground, then a second cluster far in the distance, reading as two separate small armies rather than one massive continuous one; the 'reserve box' language also collapsed the Macedonian side into a small drilled square — dropped entirely this version). CRITICAL RULE: each army is ONE unbroken continuous mass along its own depth — there is NO empty ground inside either army's own footprint between its nearest and farthest visible ranks. The only permitted break in either formation is the single specific torn-gap feature described below — never a second large empty area. High aerial angle, close to straight-down; army coverage fills nearly the entire frame, with only ONE narrow strip of true open ground in the whole image — the no-man's-land directly between the two facing fronts. MACEDONIAN SIDE (nearer band): one continuous deep mass with no internal breaks — Craterus's pike phalanx in the center, sarissa points dense and unbroken; Alexander's Companion cavalry and hypaspists massed at the near-right edge of that same continuous body, already peeling off at a diagonal into the forming wedge; Parmenion's Thessalian cavalry massed at the left edge of the same body, held slightly back. All of it reads as one large touching army, not separate clusters. PERSIAN SIDE (rest of frame, to the horizon): one continuous deep mass, dramatically WIDER than the Macedonian side and extending well past both Macedonian flanks — light two-horse scythed chariots screening its leading edge merge directly into the massed ranks immediately behind them, touching, NOT a separate cluster with empty ground before the next; Darius and his elite guard (Immortals, Greek mercenaries) hold the center within this same continuous body; distinct cavalry wings are visible under different banners within it — Bessus's Bactrian/Scythian/Dahae cavalry nearer Alexander's advance, shown in motion, shifting to chase him; Mazaeus's Median/Parthian/Armenian cavalry on the far wing, banners and dress visibly different. The ONE permitted break: a gap — thinner, paler ranks, still part of the same continuous body, not a separate empty field — visible in the Persian center-left where Bessus's troops are shifting to chase Alexander's wing. Historical scale for density: Macedonian force ~47,000 in one compact, deep, unbroken formation; Persian force by the most-cited modern scholarly estimates (not the inflated ancient figures) roughly 90,000–100,000, several times wider and equally unbroken in depth.

Because both subjects sit at roughly the same camera distance, their ground-contact points land at the same height in frame by ordinary perspective, so the 'two floors' problem never arises and there is nothing for a video model to fuse. Verified at the pixel level: continuous dirt/dust texture connects the horse's hoof-contact point to the soldiers' feet with no seam, no collage edge, no mesh artifact. LEFT THIRD: a dark bay Macedonian cavalry horse's lower legs and hooves at full gallop, hoof striking the ground with dust bursting at the contact point — no saddle, no rider, no stirrup (a bridle/rein across the horse's head/neck is visible, consistent with a ridden warhorse, not a violation). Her eyes are level and direct on the lens, unbroken. The wax tablet remains held low at her side, calm, out of her sightline. Background: campfires relighting scattered through the deep frame behind her, deepening blue-hour sky, small warm lights in darkness echoing Clip 1's opening. EYELINE: her eyes are on the lens for this entire still, unwavering, direct — continuing the unbroken gaze from 9a into this new beat.
